issues.description: Method addGuestStudents(int): The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares addGuestStudents(int) with a void return type, but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) defines public boolean addGuestStudents(int). The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) only contains a TODO for adding addGuestStudents and does not specify a signature. This mismatch between the UML and the solution confuses students about the intended method contract (should callers expect a boolean success flag or no return value) and can cause inconsistencies when students implement the method or when automated graders check the API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents(int) signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution implementation to match the UML and template intent by declaring public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and update its body to perform the addition without returning a value; or (B) Update the problem statement UML and the template TODO to declare addGuestStudents(int): boolean and document the meaning of the boolean return value (e.g., true when addition succeeded, false otherwise). Ensure the template file includes the chosen signature so students implement the correct return type.
